hooks.command:
jq -c '{systemMessage: ((.tool_name | sub("mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__";"")) + ":
" + (if (.tool_input.commands | type) == "array" then ([.tool_input.commands[]? | "  • " + (.label // "") + ": " + .command] | join("
")) else "  " + (if .tool_input.path then "[" + .tool_input.path + "] " else "" end) + "(" + (.tool_input.language // "?") + ")
" + (.tool_input.code // "(no code)") end)), hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "allow", permissionDecisionReason: "context-mode ctx_* auto-approved"}}'
jq -c '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "allow", permissionDecisionReason: "context-mode read-only ctx_* auto-approved"}}'
jq -c '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "allow", permissionDecisionReason: "drawio read-only tool auto-approved"}}'

//hooks.PreToolUse[ctx-observer]: Prints ctx_execute/ctx_execute_file/ctx_batch_execute inputs as systemMessage AND returns permissionDecision:allow to auto-approve these sandbox/read tools. Why: plan mode ignores permissions.allow, so the ctx_* wildcard alone still prompts every call; the hook allow skips the prompt while keeping plan mode. Scope is limited to context-mode ctx_*execute (matcher); all other tools stay under normal plan-mode gating. settings.json is strict JSON (no // or /* */ comments); this dummy key is the JSON-safe way to annotate. See .claude/plans/ctx-batch-execute-eager-dawn.md
//hooks.PreToolUse[ctx-readonly-allow]: Same plan-mode workaround as ctx-observer, for the retrieval-side ctx_* tools whose tool_input shape (requests/queries/path) the observer's jq formatter cannot render. Kept as a separate entry so the formatter stays untouched: if that jq ever exits non-zero the hook output is discarded and the allow is lost with it. Destructive or state-changing tools (ctx_purge, ctx_upgrade) are deliberately excluded and stay under normal gating.
//hooks.PreToolUse[drawio-readonly-allow: Same plan-mode workaround again, for the read-only tools of the drawio MCP server. Why: drawing an infrastructure diagram means calling search_shapes many times in a row to resolve vendor icon styles, and plan mode ignores the mcp__drawio__* entry in permissions.allow, so every lookup would prompt. set_page (writes a .drawio file) and open_drawio_xml (launches an external browser) are deliberately excluded and stay under normal gating.
//mcpServers: Left empty on purpose. Claude Code does not read mcpServers from settings.json — an entry here never shows up in `claude mcp list`. User-scoped servers live in ~/.claude.json, which .chezmoiignore excludes, so they are declared in .chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_claude-mcp-servers.sh instead.
